w: Built in 1577 over the ruins of an older church, this cathedral was rebuilt in Baroque style in the 18th century and became seat of the Metropolis of Corfu in 1841. It holds the icon of Panagia Spilaiotissa and the relics of Saint Theodora, brought from Constantinople in 1460.
s: Corfu's cathedral, home to relics fled from Byzantium
_facts: Cathedral of the Metropolis of Corfu, Paxoi and the Diapontian Islands
Built 1577 on the ruins of an ancient church; rebuilt in Baroque style in the 18th century
Became cathedral of the Holy Metropolis in 1841
Houses the icon of Panagia Spilaiotissa and relics of Saint Theodora, brought from Constantinople in 1460

w: Empress Elisabeth of Austria built this palace at Gastouri as a refuge after the 1889 Mayerling death of her son, Crown Prince Rudolf. She styled it around Achilles, evoking mythical Phaeacia, sited for views of Corfu city and the Ionian Sea. It's now a museum.
s: A grieving empress's palace themed on Achilles
_facts: Palace built for Empress Elisabeth of Austria after the 1889 Mayerling death of her son Crown Prince Rudolf
Located at Gastouri, about 10 km south of Corfu city
Architecture themed around the hero Achilles, evoking mythical Phaeacia
Now a museum under the Greek National Tourism Organization

w: This tiny islet - its name means 'Mouse Island' - carries an 11th- or 12th-century Byzantine chapel to Christ Pantokrator, and may have inspired Bocklin's Isle of the Dead. Naturalist Gerald Durrell, who swam out to it as a Corfu boy, had his ashes scattered here.
s: The islet that may have inspired Isle of the Dead
_facts: Greek islet whose name means 'Mouse Island'
Byzantine chapel of Christ Pantokrator dating from the 11th or 12th century
Possible inspiration for Bocklin's painting Isle of the Dead
Ashes of naturalist Gerald Durrell and his sister Margaret were scattered here

w: At 906 metres, this is Corfu's highest point, topped by a monastery whose first version, built by the Angevins in 1347, was destroyed around 1537; today's church dates to about 1689. On a clear day the view stretches past Albania as far as Italy, 130 km off.
s: Corfu's highest peak, views clear to Italy
_facts: Highest mountain on Corfu at 906 metres, in the northeast of the island
Summit views take in all of Corfu, Albania, and on clear days Italy (about 130 km away)
First monastery built 1347 by the Angevins, destroyed c. 1537; current church c. 1689
Old Perithia, Corfu's oldest village, is a common starting point for the walk up

w: This former royal summer residence sits in the forest of Palaeopolis, just south of Corfu City. Since 2001 it has housed the Museum of Palaiopolis - Mon Repos, turning a private retreat into public ground for the ancient city beneath it.
s: A royal summer villa turned archaeology museum
_facts: Former royal summer residence on Corfu, south of Corfu City in the forest of Palaeopolis
Since 2001, houses the Museum of Palaiopolis - Mon Repos

w: Raised around 580 BC in ancient Korkyra, this was one of the first Doric temples built entirely of stone, among the first to unite every element of the Doric style. Excavated from 1911 at the Saint Theodore monastery, it yielded rare Archaic pediment sculpture.
s: One of the first all-stone Doric temples
_facts: Archaic Greek temple built c. 580 BC in ancient Korkyra (Corfu), dedicated to Artemis
One of the first Doric temples built exclusively of stone
Excavated from 1911 on the grounds of the Saint Theodore monastery, Garitsa
Yielded some of the earliest surviving large fragments of Archaic pediment sculpture

w: The Venetians dug the Contrafossa, a sea channel, to cut this promontory off from the city and turn their citadel into an artificial island. It worked: the fortress repelled Ottoman sieges in 1537, 1571 and 1716. Its twin peaks - 'Coryphe' in Greek - gave Corfu its name.
s: The twin-peaked fortress that gave Corfu its name
_facts: Venetian fortress (Fortezza Vecchia) built over earlier Byzantine fortifications
The Contrafossa moat separated the promontory into an artificial island
Repelled Ottoman sieges in 1537, 1571 and 1716
The name 'Corfu' derives from the fortress's twin peaks, 'Coryphe' in Greek

n: Cathedral of Saint James and Saint Christopher
w: Seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Corfu, Zakynthos and Cephalonia, this cathedral - known locally as the Duomo - holds an extensive painting collection, centered on the Virgin Vrefokratousa Enthroned, painted in 1654 by Konstantinos Tzanes.
s: Corfu's Catholic cathedral, known as the Duomo
_facts: Seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Corfu, Zakynthos and Cephalonia
Also known as the Catholic Metropolitan Church or the Duomo
Houses the Virgin Vrefokratousa Enthroned, painted 1654 by Konstantinos Tzanes

w: Built in stages on the hill of St. Mark, this Venetian fortress was laid out by engineer Ferrante Vitelli, then rebuilt by the British during their rule, 1815 to 1863. It once carried 700 pieces of artillery; part of it now serves as the Naval Station of Corfu's headquarters.
s: A Venetian fort rebuilt by the British, still a naval HQ
_facts: Venetian fortress (Fortezza Nuova) on the hill of St. Mark, originally by engineer Ferrante Vitelli
Current buildings largely built by the British during their rule, 1815-1863
Once held 700 pieces of artillery
A building within it now serves as headquarters of the Naval Station of Corfu

w: Facing directly onto the Old Fortress, this esplanade is the largest square in Greece and the biggest in Europe - the 27th largest in the world by area. It forms the vast open heart of Corfu Town, dwarfing even the fortress across from it.
s: Europe's biggest square, facing the Old Fortress
_facts: Large central square in Corfu, whose name means 'esplanade'
Largest square in Greece, biggest in Europe, 27th biggest in the world by area
Sits directly in front of the Old Fortress

w: For 41 years, from 1902 until a Luftwaffe raid destroyed it in 1943, this was one of Greece's premier opera houses, billed as the first theatre in Southeastern Europe. It succeeded the older Nobile Teatro di San Giacomo, later repurposed as Corfu's city hall.
s: The opera house the Luftwaffe destroyed in 1943
_facts: Main theatre and opera house in Corfu from 1902 to 1943
Successor to the Nobile Teatro di San Giacomo di Corfu, which became the city hall
Destroyed by a German Luftwaffe bombing raid in 1943
Billed as the first theatre in Southeastern Europe

w: Built between 1962 and 1965 on land donated by the city, this museum was created to house finds from the nearby Temple of Artemis. A 1994 expansion added two more halls for material from the ancient citadel of Corfu.
s: Built to house the Temple of Artemis's finds
_facts: Built 1962-1965 on land donated by the city of Corfu
Originally created to house finds from the Temple of Artemis
Expanded 1994 with two more halls for finds from the ancient citadel of Corfu

n: Palace of St. Michael and St. George
w: Commissioned by Sir Thomas Maitland as residence of the British Lord High Commissioner of the Ionian Islands, this neoclassical palace rose 1819 to 1824, designed by Colonel George Whitmore. Locals still call it Palaia Anaktora - the Old Palace.
_facts: Commissioned by Sir Thomas Maitland as residence of the British Lord High Commissioner of the Ionian Islands
Built 1819-1824, neoclassical design by Colonel George Whitmore
Also known as the Royal Palace, City Palace, or Palaia Anaktora

w: Housed in the former church of the Holy Mother of God Antivouniotissa - the name means 'facing the mountain' - this museum specializes in post-Byzantine religious art from the Cretan and early Heptanese schools, in a deconsecrated building that's part of the exhibit.
s: Post-Byzantine icons in a deconsecrated church
_facts: Museum of post-Byzantine religious art, Cretan and early Heptanese schools
Located in the former church of the Holy Mother of God Antivouniotissa

w: Built in 1589 in the old town, this single-nave basilica is Corfu's most famous church, built to house the relics of Saint Spyridon. Its bell tower, added in 1620, is the tallest in the Ionian Islands.
s: Corfu's most famous church, holds Saint Spyridon's relics
_facts: Greek Orthodox church built in 1589, houses the relics of Saint Spyridon
Single-nave basilica; the most famous church in Corfu
Bell tower, built 1620, is the tallest in the Ionian Islands

w: Built by a ruler of the Despotate of Epirus in the 13th century, this is the only medieval fortress surviving on Corfu's southern coast. Before the Venetians arrived in 1401, three castles formed a defensive triangle: Gardiki in the south, Kassiopi in the northeast, Angelokastro in the northwest.
s: One corner of Corfu's pre-Venetian defence triangle
_facts: 13th-century Byzantine castle on Corfu's southwestern coast
Only surviving medieval fortress on the southern part of the island
Built by a ruler of the Despotate of Epirus
One of three castles (with Kassiopi and Angelokastro) defending the island before the Venetian era (1401-1797)
